statements.text: [[revenue|Revenue]] was about the same as the year before, at $46.4 billion in the year ended May 31, 2026.
In the [[quarter|quarter]] ended August 31, 2026, revenue was $11.2 billion, down 4.3% from the same quarter a year earlier.
[[net-income|Net income]], the profit left after all costs and taxes, fell 3.4% to $3.1 billion in the year ended May 31, 2026.
After paying for the products it sold, the company kept about $43 of every $100 of sales. This is called its [[gross-margin|gross margin]].
Out of every $100 of sales, about $7 was left as profit after all costs and taxes. This is called its [[profit-margin|profit margin]].
Its day-to-day business brought in $2.9 billion of cash in the year ended May 31, 2026. This is called [[cash-from-operations|cash from operations]].
On August 31, 2026, the company had $6.9 billion in [[cash-and-equivalents|cash and cash equivalents]], money it can use quickly.
On August 31, 2026, it owed $5.9 billion in [[long-term-debt|long-term debt due after the next 12 months]].

figures.label: long-term debt due after the next 12 months

statements.text: On that date it held more in cash than it owed in long-term debt.

figures.label: long-term debt due after the next 12 months

statements.text: On August 31, 2026, the company had $23.7 billion in cash and other assets it expects to use within a year, against $11.4 billion of bills due within a year. That is about $2.07 for every $1 it owes soon, more than enough to cover them. This is its [[current-ratio|current ratio]].
It owned $37.8 billion in [[assets|assets]] and owed $22.6 billion in [[total-liabilities|total liabilities]], so it owned about $1.67 for every $1 it owed.

figures.label: total liabilities (worked out as liabilities and equity, minus equity, from the balance sheet)

statements.text: For every $1 of [[shareholders-equity|shareholders' equity]] ($15.2 billion), it owed about $0.39 in long-term debt ($5.9 billion). This is its [[debt-to-equity|debt-to-equity ratio]].

figures.label: long-term debt due after the next 12 months

statements.text: Its business brought in $2.9 billion of cash in the year ended May 31, 2026 and spent $684 million on [[capital-expenditure|buildings and equipment]], leaving $2.2 billion of [[free-cash-flow|free cash flow]]: money it could use for dividends, buybacks, paying down debt or growing.
Free cash flow was smaller than its [[net-income|net income]] ($3.1 billion) that year, meaning less of its accounting profit turned into spare cash.

In the year ended May 31, 2026, the company spent $146 million buying back its own shares ([[share-buyback|buybacks]]), paid $2.4 billion in [[dividend|dividends]] to shareholders and invested $684 million in buildings and equipment.
It earned about $22 of profit for every $100 of [[shareholders-equity|shareholders' equity]] in the year ended May 31, 2026. This is its [[return-on-equity|return on equity]] (22.1%).
[[eps|Earnings per share]] (diluted) fell 2.8% to $2.10 in the year ended May 31, 2026.
Over the 5 years to May 31, 2026, its [[gross-margin|gross margin]] fell to 42.9%, from 46%.
In the year to May 2026, it made $46.4 billion in [[revenue|sales]], about the same as the year before. Sales in its latest three months (to August 2026) were down 4.3% on a year earlier.
In the year to May 2026, it kept $3.1 billion as [[net-income|profit]] after paying all its costs and taxes: about $7 of every $100 it made in sales, its [[profit-margin|profit margin]].

On August 31, 2026, for every $1 of bills due within a year, it had about $2.07 in cash and other things it expected to turn into cash in that time: more than enough to cover them. This is its [[current-ratio|current ratio]].
On August 31, 2026, it owed $5.9 billion in [[long-term-debt|loans and bonds]] not due for repayment within a year and held $6.9 billion in [[cash-and-equivalents|cash]].

statements.text: In the year to May 2026, its everyday business brought in $2.9 billion in [[cash-from-operations|cash]]. After paying for [[capital-expenditure|new buildings and equipment]], $2.2 billion was [[free-cash-flow|left over]].

In the year to May 2026, its biggest uses of money were: paying [[dividend|dividends]] to shareholders: $2.4 billion; [[capital-expenditure|new buildings and equipment]]: $684 million; and [[share-buyback|buying back its own shares]]: $146 million.

wikipedia.title: Nike, Inc.
wikipedia.extract: Nike, Inc. is an American athletic footwear and apparel corporation headquartered near Beaverton, Oregon. It is the world's largest supplier of athletic shoes and apparel and a major manufacturer of sports equipment, with revenue in excess of US$46 billion in its fiscal year 2022.
